clue.text: Report one new bird — a peacock?

parts.note: a report is a bang, a pop
the Roman numeral for one is I
the jay is a noisy bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher logs a new bird and wonders if it was a peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as figurative: a peacock here is a vain, showy person, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a vain, strutting dandy who shows off his finery.

clue.text: Host removed, so to speak, from party in US

indicators.note: re-moved punningly read as RE moved away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the Republicans are one of the two main US political parties

explanation.surface: A host is thrown out of an American political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' asks you to hear 'removed' as RE-moved: RE is taken off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican, the landlord of a pub, is the host who welcomes and serves customers.

clue.text: Social barrier that divides neighbours

parts.note: a social is a party, a gathering
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Neighbours argue over a social barrier between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A party wall is the shared wall between two adjoining houses, separating the households on either side.

clue.text: Jog, like a streaker, around midnight

indicators.note: the word for unclothed goes around the middle letter

parts.note: a streaker runs naked, nude
the middle of night is its middle letter, G

explanation.surface: A streaker goes jogging in the dead of night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' reads as running, fitting the streaker, but means a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to nudge it, a light push.

clue.text: One related, say, information that produces defensive reaction

indicators.note: say tells you the relative's name is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: an auntie is a relative
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A relative gives information that provokes a defensive response.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a substance that triggers the body's immune system to make antibodies.

clue.text: Moralist's telegraphic message for sailor

definitions.meaning: a moralist's verdict in clipped telegram style: wrongdoing, no good
the seafaring hero of the Arabian Nights tales

explanation.surface: A preacher wires a terse warning to a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the name reads as a terse telegram condemning wrongdoing; whole, it is the voyager of the Thousand and One Nights.

clue.text: Transient changes immediately resulting

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word are moved about

explanation.surface: A fleeting thing alters at once as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transient' looks like a near synonym of the definition, but its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a formal or legal word for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Not a main thoroughfare? It is in Oxford

definitions.meaning: a lesser road is a ..., not a main A road in British road classification
... Street in Oxford is known simply as the ...

explanation.surface: A minor road runs through Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: A roads are main routes, B roads lesser ones. Broad Street, beside Balliol in Oxford, is called the Broad.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as B ROAD it is a minor route; whole, it is the Oxford street known as the Broad.

clue.text: More or less dotty cloak

definitions.meaning: a tile marked with spots, from none to six, so more or less spotted
a hooded cloak worn with a mask at masquerades

explanation.surface: A rather eccentric cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spotted game tile and a loose masquerade cloak with a hood.

clue.text: Means for producing pictures occurred to artist

parts.note: came can mean occurred, as in 'it came to me'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A way of making pictures occurred to a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device used to take photographs.

clue.text: A ringleader in plot is revealed

indicators.note: the letters of a and the ring's leader go inside the word for plot

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
the leader of ring is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: The instigator of a conspiracy has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' reads as the plotter, but it means only the first letter of 'ring'; 'plot' is a garden bed, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover it, so bared is a synonym of exposed.

clue.text: Change partners, since in vehicle

indicators.note: the partners and the word for since are placed within the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle on rails
North and South are partners at bridge, N and S
for can mean since, as in 'for it was late'

explanation.surface: Someone swaps dancing partners because they are riding in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are bridge partners: North and South play together against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to alter completely, a synonym of change as a verb.

clue.text: Girl with long way to go in high-class university set

parts.note: Ivy is a girl's name
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A girl with a long journey ahead is heading for an elite university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of old, prestigious universities in the north-eastern United States.

clue.text: Poet has Goldsmith's material to study

parts.note: a goldsmith works gold, chemical symbol Au
a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: A poet owns study material from Oliver Goldsmith.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith reads as the writer Oliver Goldsmith, fitting the poetic surface, but it means a worker in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Some players on leave

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, so some players are a band
taken as written

explanation.surface: A few team members are away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a noun (time off) but is the verb, to desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to desert them, one sense of leave as a verb.

clue.text: Hated new carriage creating dangerous situation

indicators.note: new says the letters of the word are made into something fresh

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: A loathed new carriage puts its passengers in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns HATED into DEATH; a trap is a small horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is a place or vehicle so unsafe it could kill.

clue.text: Voice, possibly, I have on legislation

indicators.note: in a down-the-page reading of the charade, one word goes on, that is after, the other

parts.note: an act is a law passed by a legislature
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone states they have a say on a new law.
explanation.walkthrough: Grammar has an active and a passive voice; 'possibly' says active is one example of a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The active is one of the two grammatical voices of verbs, the other being passive.

clue.text: Wins against one hundred politicians

parts.note: V for versus means against
the Roman numeral for one is I
the Roman numeral for a hundred is C
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Election wins are scored against a hundred politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories are successes, the plural noun matching wins.

clue.text: Divinity can be puzzle, I assume

parts.note: to pose a question is to puzzle someone
to don a garment is to assume it

explanation.surface: A theologian is baffled by a puzzle about the divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, a deity.

clue.text: Start to grow one inside, yielding plenty

indicators.note: one is placed inside the word for starting something growing

parts.note: to plant is to set something in the ground to start it growing
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A seedling begins to grow, and one plant inside produces a big crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plenty' reads as part of the picture of a harvest and acts only as a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliant bends easily, so it is supple and gives way under pressure.

clue.text: Calamitous end of aircraft shown by rising smoke

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter
in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cigar is a smoke

explanation.surface: A disastrous end for a plane, marked by smoke climbing skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns CIGAR upwards to RAGIC in this down clue; 'end of aircraft' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something disastrous, a synonym of calamitous.

clue.text: Jack leading heroic characters into walled town

indicators.note: Jack comes first, leading the rest of the letters

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: the letters, the characters, of heroic are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man named Jack leads a band of heroes into a fortified town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in a story; here it means the letters of 'heroic', which are rearranged and placed after Jack's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city whose walls fell to Joshua's trumpets is the classic walled town.

clue.text: Various creatures Alice upset in trying circumstances

definitions.text: Various creatures Alice upset in trying circumstances

parts.words: Various creatures Alice upset in trying circumstances
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the animals in the jury box at the Knave's trial are tipped over by Alice; trying means at a trial

explanation.surface: Alice upsets various animals in a difficult situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' sounds like 'difficult' but means 'at a trial': in Wonderland, Alice knocks over the jury box at the Knave of Hearts' trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of a jury sitting on a court case were the animals Alice spilled.

clue.text: Disorder occurs in plant

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of the following word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some disease turns up in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small bulb flower that blooms in early spring.

clue.text: Name in order, alphabetically

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A list of names is set out in alphabetical order.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits across the end of 'order' and the start of 'alphabetically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a man's first name.

clue.text: Reduce the glare

definitions.meaning: to scowl or frown, also spelt lour

explanation.surface: Turn down the harsh light.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to bring down and, said to rhyme with flour, to scowl or look threatening.

clue.text: Craft are moored in a landing-place

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion, so the letters of the words are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Aircraft are parked up at an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a noun, aircraft, but is a verb telling you to fashion the letters of 'are moored' anew.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is an airfield, a place where aircraft touch down.

clue.text: Latecomer's last in joint effort

indicators.note: the final letter is placed inside the word for joint

parts.note: a joint or dive is a seedy bar or club

indicators.note: last says only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A latecomer finally joins a team effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' reads as shared, but it is a noun: a cheap, disreputable bar, a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is an organised campaign, an energetic push to achieve something.

clue.text: Mr Winkle, for example, is a master of the dramatic bon-mot

parts.note: Nathaniel Winkle in Dickens's Pickwick Papers is a faint-hearted sportsman who dodges a duel
taken as written
M is an abbreviation for master, as in an MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is praised as a great wit of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Winkle is the timid sportsman of Dickens's Pickwick Papers. The definition plays on Noel Coward, playwright famous for witty one-liners: a Coward-ism.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage for a witty saying in the manner of the playwright Noel Coward, master of the stage epigram.

clue.text: From Irish house I brought back epic tale

indicators.note: brought back says the Irish house and I are read in reverse order and letters

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A traveller brings home an epic story from an Irish home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns the whole run DAILI round; 'Irish house' is the parliament chamber, not a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is the archetypal epic.

clue.text: Angelic sort, perhaps, losing one penny in change

indicators.note: the word perhaps is put through a change, rearranged after a letter goes

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone saintly, perhaps, is a penny short when given change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' links the two: drop P from PERHAPS, leaving ERHAPS, and rearrange that. 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge on the definition but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels.

clue.text: Senselessness of a French cause

parts.note: un is French for a
a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: Someone laments the folly of a French cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is a lack of rational thought, irrationality.
